answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Fingerprint. Each identity’s action sequence is hashed into a per-epoch vector; agents must reproduce prior-epoch similarity above a fixed threshold, checked at a random vertex in the interaction graph. A juniper flag marks identities whose cross-epoch drift exceeds tolerance, suspending them pending review. Sybils must maintain distinct histories across epochs, so each duplicate requires continuous independent behaviour generation. A whisper of coordination collapses the cluster when histories correlate.
